title: Rome, January 1478 st. fior. (1479): Giovanni Mazzinghi and an unsigned writer to the Medici, word-by-word cipher (ASF MAP LXXXIX 142, CXXXVII 252; key source MAP LXXII 170)

documents.shelfmark: ASF, Mediceo avanti il Principato LXXXIX 142
documents.date: 16 January 1478 st. fior. ("In nome di Dio a dì xvj di gennaio 1478"; place not stated, Rome by content)

plaintext.source: Bare: no decipherment on or beside the leaf (vetting batch n08).

transcription.notes: 209 cipher words, 1,066 signs after joining 2+/2# to one l-sign (measure.py); words rechecked at 5-6x (recheck.tsv).

documents.shelfmark: ASF, Mediceo avanti il Principato CXXXVII 252
documents.route: unsigned (same hand and signs as 2307) -> the Medici

transcription.notes: 121 cipher words, 581 signs after joining 2+/2# (measure.py); words rechecked at 5-6x (recheck.tsv).

system.summary: Homophonic letter substitution in letter-like signs (several for each vowel), word by word with word division kept and clear words between; numerals as code words for persons.
system.sibling_key: MAP LXXII 170, same signs, with a contemporary interlinear decipherment

prior_solution.where: No decipherment of 2307 or 2320 on the leaves, in Lorenzo's Lettere II-IV, or by web search; the sibling LXXII 170 carries its own contemporary decipherment, used as key material.

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau chose the target; the model does the work. A second session worked 2307 from the catalogue task prompt (ciphertext only) at the same time; no target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Full-size images of MAP LXXXIX 142, CXXXVII 252, LXXII 170 and neighbours downloaded from the ASF MAP viewer (getdoc.py).
Datelines read: all three 'gennaio 1478', i.e. January 1479 modern (Florentine style); 2307 headed 'In Roma'; LXXII 170 verso is show-through only.

Glyph inventory (glyphs.md, 45 tokens) and transcription of the glossed sibling MAP LXXII 170 with its interlinear decipherment (t170.tsv: 194 cipher words, 154 with a gloss, 73 of them h/m confidence); glosses drift left of their words and were assigned by word order.

Key fitted on 69 confident cipher-word/gloss pairs of LXXII 170 by hard-EM monotone alignment (build_key.py, key.tsv): homophonic letter substitution with word division kept, e.g. + a, x/y e, s/5/1/3 i, r o, n n, H t, 6 r, o d, q u, {sg} c, 2+ l, p p, 4 s, 8 m, m g, = b; numerals are code words for persons. Held-out fifth over four splits: 57-74% of letters, limited by the glosses' legibility and alignment.

Sign-by-sign transcription of the two bare letters with the 170 token set plus new tokens (glyphs.md 'New in 252/142'): MAP CXXXVII 252 (t252.tsv: 14 lines, 121 cipher words, 595 signs, 7 clear words, 4 numerals) and MAP LXXXIX 142 (t142.tsv: 37 lines, 209 cipher words, 1109 signs, 132 clear words, 13 numerals). New tokens {dbar} {3bar} {eq3} {Hp} {B} {h} {pbar} {T} {nn} {phi} {/o/}; {Hp} is the form 170 transcribed # in 'letere'. No decipherment or gloss on either letter. The 142 dateline reads '+ In nom[e] d[i] d[io] a dì xvj di gennaio 1478', not 'In Roma'.
Bare letters transcribed with the same tokens: t252.tsv (121 cipher words, 595 signs) and t142.tsv (209 cipher words, 1,109 signs); new signs {Hp}, {dbar}, {pbar}, {T} and others added to glyphs.md.

Signs absent from the glossed pairs given values by it-cinquecento 5-gram hill-climbing over both letters (refine.py), then fixed by word context where the LM chose badly: {pbar}/{dbar} p, {Hp} tt, b f, g ss, c e (key_refined.tsv).

Draft decryption of both bare letters (draft252.txt, draft142.txt) reads as Italian through most words: 252 on a papal brief and fear that Antonio del Palagio, Pagolo Rucellai and Lionardo di Giunta will be seized; 142 (Mazzinghi) on a bull annulling privileges, a cruel process against the Medici, and Iacopo de' Rossi da Pistoia and a Pistoiese called Cola, with 'ordinò la morte di [30]'. Look-alike signs (o/q, #/h, t) still misread in places.

Recheck of doubtful signs in 252 and 142 against the images at 4-6x (recheck.tsv, crops/recheck/): 112 words checked, 53 supported, 11 not supported, 48 unclear; 46 transcription corrections. Settled: the c-sign (sigma) also writes q (cuesta) and most o-read-as-c cases were a missed sigma; h has no shape of its own (double cross after c or g = ch/gh); '2 #' = l; t = {dbar} = {pbar} (barred p: p in words, 'per' standing alone); new {2bar} (z with top bar) = o; 3 = ss; six b were 6 (r); 2+ often written like 4. Clear abbreviations of 142 lines 18-37 expanded in clear142.txt with doubts marked.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1253 tokens, 45 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -2.269 per letter; random keys -4.12 (z 4.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.742 (mean -2.757, z 31.6); annealer on the real text -2.5. Verdict: weak.
Sign-by-sign recheck of 112 doubtful words at 5-6x (recheck.tsv): 53 supported, 11 not, 48 unclear; sign classes settled ({sg} c/q, # after c/g = h, 2# = l, t = barred p, 3 = ss).
Look-alike variants (one or two sign swaps) of the 92 unread words tested against a 15th-16th c. Italian word list (variants.py): a few short words recovered, the long ones match nothing.
Reading and translation of both letters (reading.md); 76.1% of cipher signs read, measured (measure.py).
Parallel session (PR #301), 2307 without the sibling key: First pass of 89/142, 29 sign classes, 1055 signs.
Parallel session (PR #301), 2307 without the sibling key: Paired the 72/170 gloss with its cipher; only 'publichamente mostra lectere' aligned with confidence.
Parallel session (PR #301), 2307 without the sibling key: Homophonic annealer on it-cinquecento; collapsed onto all-i.
Parallel session (PR #301), 2307 without the sibling key: Same with a letter-frequency KL penalty and swap moves; Italian came out (contra di voi molto crudele, molte volte, grandissimo).
Parallel session (PR #301), 2307 without the sibling key: 537-sign Italian passage in a random 29-sign homophonic key: 655/667 letters right.
Parallel session (PR #301), 2307 without the sibling key: Second transcription pass in 3x crops and word-by-word reading; merged sign classes resolved from context.

Every Medici key sheet of 1472-1494 in MAP LXXII 178-189 bis and CXIX 115-127 (plus LXXII 172, 209-210, CXXIV 184) compared with the rebuilt key for the code list: none is this cipher (keysheets.md). The same check found a third letter in this cipher, MAP CXXXVII 63 (catalogue 2321), not read here.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.269; polyphony 0.0; 394 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.5

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The key was fitted on the contemporary interlinear decipherment of a different letter in the same cipher (MAP LXXII 170, January 1478/9), then completed from context; neither 2307 nor 2320 carries any decipherment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: measure.py on t252.tsv + t142.tsv: 1,253 of 1,647 cipher signs in words that read as sense (252: 371/581, 142: 882/1,066); unread words listed in measure.py.

gaps.item: 92 cipher words (394 signs) that do not decode to sense, listed in measure.py UNREAD
gaps.detail: signs are 8-14 px at the ASF server's maximum (1272 px wide); rechecked at 5-6x (recheck.tsv) and tested against look-alike variants (variants.py); no higher-resolution image online

gaps.item: code numerals 10, 30, 40, 51, 231, 10/3 and the recurring group OLDP/DLDP/EDP
gaps.detail: only 12 = Zanobi is glossed in LXXII 170; the gloss over 10 reads 'Duca' plus an illegible word; none of the Medici key sheets of 1472-1494 (MAP LXXII 178-189 bis, CXIX 115-127, LXXII 172, 209-210, CXXIV 184) is this cipher (keysheets.md)

credits.note: The interlinear decipherment of MAP LXXII 170, written in January 1478/9, gave the cipher-word / plain-word pairs the key was fitted on.

texts.label: MAP CXXXVII 252, 13 January 1478 st. fior. (1479), unsigned
texts.summary: An unsigned writer in Rome, three days before Mazzinghi's letter: the Pope has sent a brief, a letter was presented to [10], and the king is so enraged that the writer fears Antonio del Palagio, Pagolo Rucellai and Lionardo di Giunta, Florentines in Rome, will be seized and put in Castel Sant'Angelo; written in haste during the Pazzi War.

reading_review.note: Sentences form in most lines; lines 2-3 and 6 have several unread words in a row; 64% of signs read.

texts.label: MAP LXXXIX 142, Giovanni Mazzinghi, 16 January 1478 st. fior. (1479)
texts.summary: Giovanni Mazzinghi warns the Medici from Rome: a bull under lead has been published in the Chancery revoking the privileges the Church had granted, a very cruel process is being made against them, and Iacopo de' Rossi of Pistoia and another Pistoiese, Cola, are involved in a plot ('quello ordino la morte di [30]', 'ogni cosa fanno per la vostra fine'). Nine months after the Pazzi conspiracy, during the war and the interdict.

reading_review.note: Lines 1-18 build sentences with scattered holes; lines 18-37 mix clear abbreviations and cipher and read in stretches; 83% of signs read.

outcome.notes: Dated 'gennaio 1478' in Florentine style, i.e. January 1479. Key from the sibling's contemporary gloss (external plaintext); no prior reading found.
